summary: myidsan's account chip now opens a single self-service "Profile" page consolidating change-password, TOTP MFA management, and a new profile-picture (avatar) editor -- it is a chipOnly route reached only from the account chip in the side rail, never a nav item or dashboard tile, so it doesn't compete for menu space. This ships myidsan's first in-app self-service change-password form (POST /api/login/default/change-password), previously reachable only via the forced first-login screen. Profile pictures are a new UserAvatar entity (one base64-JPEG row per account, never carried in JWT/session claims) and a profileApi surface: self-service GET/POST/DELETE /api/profile/avatar (auth-only, own account) plus a superadmin GET/POST/DELETE /api/profile/avatar/{userId} surface that lets an operator set or clear any user's picture inline from the Users management page (a new per-row avatar + camera button). The client center-crops and resizes the picked image to a 256px JPEG in-browser (canvas) before upload, so the server needs no image codec -- just a MIME allow-list (JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF) and a 512KB decoded-size cap; a missing avatar is a plain 404 the SPA renders as an initials fallback. Three icons (mail, upload, shield-check) were added to the shared frontend icon set to support the new page. Also fixes a CSS bug where the workspace-header theme dropdown stretched full-width across the content area and could open off-screen; it is now content-sized and opens downward, right-aligned -- a visual bug fix with no behavior or API change.
compatibility: Purely additive. One new DB table (user_avatar, auto-added by bootstrap schema generation); no changes to any existing table, endpoint, or config default. An existing install upgrades with no avatar set for any account (SPA renders initials fallback) until a user or a superadmin uploads one. MFA and change-password behavior/routes are unchanged -- only their UI location moved (from a dedicated Account -> Security screen to the consolidated Profile page reached via the account chip).
